correctness.rationale: The frozen proof and checker give nonsquarefreeness at the witness, but divisibility by 59² alone does not show the whole gcd is squarefull. Also 1 must be excluded from the squarefull least-index claim (it satisfies the vacuous exponent condition, and occurs already at index 1). The corrected files state and verify G_29(298)=3481=59², hence both least-index conclusions, with squarefull gcd required to be nontrivial. The lower-index proof is valid: the only unit-circle pairs z,z+1 have orders three and six, so the integer resultant is nonzero; its Bézout identity bounds every gcd including if one value vanishes. Every possible square divisor has a prime in the exact factorization and lies over a common residue; the two first-order lift constraints remain valid at zero derivatives and cover all integers. Independent monic division and Bareiss Sylvester determinants verify the factorizations and 178 common roots at 97 index–prime entries, then the candidate lift (or singular-case incompatibility) at each; none lifts simultaneously. Exact integer Horner evaluation and Euclidean gcd give 3481. The repaired checker separately passed using the unchanged certificate; the original evidence was kept unchanged.
residual_risks: Exact finite proof over the stated index range using symbolic resultants; the set of witnesses at index 29 is not classified.

evidence: Sanna–Szikszai obtain infinitely many long blocks for a quadratic/cubic polynomial in which no term is coprime to all others. Cohen–Sonn's integer theorem concerns large gcds infinitely often under GRH for fixed a,b,N with varying exponent. The formula attributed to the 1995 resultant paper relates polynomial indices in an argument-composition identity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An existence theorem for long blocks gives no all-integer adjacent-pair squarefreeness conclusion. Neither the fixed-base theorem nor the cited composition formula gives simultaneous prime-square lifts or a threshold across cyclotomic indices.

evidence: Failure of squarefreeness is equivalent to existence of a simultaneous root of Φ_m(X) and Φ_m(X+1) in ℤ/p²ℤ for some prime p; nontrivial squarefullness is a stronger property of the whole gcd. Exact evaluation shows both properties for the repaired witness. De Nápoli's identity relates Φ_n(X^m) to a product over cyclotomic indices. Cohen–Sonn study gcds after evaluating at fixed bases to varying powers.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Composition at X^m and changing input exponents do not match a unit translation X↦X+1, and a size estimate for such a gcd controls neither all prime-square roots nor whether all prime exponents in a given gcd are at least two.

value.rationale: The sharp parameter is the index, not an arbitrarily bounded list of input pairs. The correction identifies the first possible repeated prime in these otherwise highly restricted adjacent gcds, uniformly for every integer input across all smaller indices, and shows that the whole first witness is a pure prime square. Distinguishing a repeated prime of the resultant from an actual simultaneous lift is substantive; the verified cutoff and witness give concrete tests for any general prime-power theory of shifted cyclotomic values.
residual_risks: The first index is determined; no asymptotic or global classification of prime powers is claimed.
